replace this file once the open items are resolved or moved to issues.

## Agreed TTT direction

* First session: start from a blank repository, install the skills, brainstorm
  an aka.ms-style URL shortener, produce the BRD, PRD, and JSONL requirements
  ledger, and create a specification template. Templates from the spec seed
  implementation, and implementation templates seed operations.
* Helium (movies) is a brownfield second lab for implementation and operations,
  because its spec and data already exist. Bring-your-own scenario comes after
  a known exercise.
* GitHub templates copy files but not history, so keep reference templates as
  facilitator fallbacks.
* Gate A means "ready to plan." Planning breaks the accepted spec into
  implementation sessions at the start of Stage 2, before coding. Review
  the session map and accept the first session's RPI plan and fit check
  before implementation. Real-project ownership remains a proposed default
  in the facilitator plan, not a universal role assignment.
* Pilot constraints confirmed on continuation: two days; Go for the
  URL-shortener redirect engine, separate from any admin/reporting UI;
  12 learners in pairs with two facilitators;
  disposable local-only labs with GitHub templates and Copilot access, no
  public deployment; internal TTT packaging with learner/facilitator
  separation and no certification claim.
* Go's selection rationale is runtime performance and Docker image size,
  not a measured benchmark claim. Storage, version pins, container build,
  and resource limits still need rehearsal decisions. The facilitator plan
  now has a proposed two-day agenda.
* Next.js is the preferred admin/reporting portal candidate, not a finalized
  stack choice. Portal scope remains open; redirect serving must not depend
  on the portal.

## Related benchmark plans (owned by Wharf)

FE uses Wharf for daily HydraFusion enterprise runs and weekly Opus and OpenAI
runs, to be charted on fe-labs.ai. The views are score, agent time, and cost,
with `score = PASS@1 - p2p_errors * 0.0025`. The methodology is in Wharf's
`docs/published-benchmarks.md`.
